recap.text: Carl and Donut draw three common utility cards, while Team Sister Ines draws an uncommon special card titled Flee, which teleports the whole squad away once. Katia pushes two Flee Cards across to Carl, warning they are consumable. The final announcement makes a fleeing keyholder lose one key at random. Quan plays Force Play, switches hands with Donut, and sends three Flee cards for three, taking two keys.

beats.headline: Team Sister Ines's draw
beats.text: After the fight, Carl and Donut collect three common utility cards, two Time Extends and a Stout, none of them one-time consumables like their Combo card. Team Sister Ines gets three cards too: the same two Time Extends and an uncommon special card titled Flee. That one can be used only once, and it teleports the whole squad away from combat. It does not say how far, or where to.
beats.gist: Team Sister Ines draws two Time Extends and a one-use Flee card that teleports the squad away.

beats.headline: Two from Katia
beats.text: Katia's deck is still thin: no mystics, no snares, only a couple of specials, and she is going totem hunting in a few hours. She pushes a pair of Flee Cards across to Carl. Take two, she says; they're consumable, so be careful. He also takes another Stout and two utilities he has not seen before, Blue Stuff for a totem's mana and Greased Lightning for a mob's speed.
beats.gist: Carl takes two Flee Cards from Katia, plus a Stout and two utilities.

beats.headline: A key for a key
beats.text: The final announcement changes one rule. Without a key, a Flee card works as it always has, teleporting the user out of a losing battle to a random place nearby, which is no help to someone guarding a door. A keyholder who flees automatically loses a key, one at random, to the opponent. That is also the only way to give a key away: start a battle and flee. Donut asks what they will do if Imani does not get a key, and Carl has been thinking on it: they will force her to fight them, Donut will use the Flee card and give her their key, and the bone key benefit on his jacket will open the door for him.
beats.gist: A fleeing keyholder loses a key, so Donut will flee a fight with Imani.

beats.headline: Three for three
beats.text: Quan plays Force Play, a mystic card Carl always assumed was dumb: pick a card in an opponent's hand, and it plays itself. Sister Ines has a Flee card in her hand. Team Quiteria flees and loses its key. Carl yells to Donut not to keep a Flee card in her hand; she has already discarded it. Then Quan swoops back and switches hands with her, three for three, all Flee cards, and casts another Force Play. Their squad flees, and its key and Team Quiteria's both go to Team Quan.
beats.gist: Quan's Force Play makes both other squads flee, and Team Quan takes their keys.

beats.headline: Jurgen flees
beats.text: The fighting has mostly calmed. Osvaldo and some guy named Jurgen got into a card battle, and Jurgen had to use a Flee card. He had really made good on his promise to break the stairwell, and now the two of them, somewhere in Brazil, are working together to clear the rubble away.
beats.gist: Jurgen uses a Flee card against Osvaldo, then the two work together clearing the stairwell rubble Jurgen made.

beats.headline: Too easy to flee
beats.text: Almost five thousand have died, and Carl knows more will before the collapse. Still, the number is shockingly low, and he sees the shape of it. They made it too easy to flee fights because they wanted these last few days to be the real slaughter, and the crawlers found a way out of it. They are hitting the ninth floor not scattered, not broken and not afraid, and in unprecedented numbers.
beats.gist: Almost five thousand have died, a low toll, because fleeing was too easy.

relations.note: forced on his opponents with Force Play
